tasks.short: Set credit policies, credit lines, procedures and standards with senior managers.

steps.what: Assemble portfolio performance, exception, complaint and loss evidence for a proposed policy change
Draft a proposed credit-line or procedure change with affected cases, controls and unresolved trade-offs

loop.input: current policy, evidence pack and stated change request
loop.output: versioned policy-change draft with cited evidence and open decisions
loop.check: the officer checks that every proposed rule and impact statement is supported by the evidence pack
loop.stop: stop on an unsupported claim, conflicting policy or missing risk owner; return the issue to the policy workshop
loop.why_not_simpler: The document has a structure, but risk appetite and policy trade-offs cannot be derived from the data.

steps.what: Debate the proposal with senior managers and approve, reject or revise the exact policy version
Publish the approved policy version and assign implementation tasks

tasks.design: A {BI} evidence pack and a {DOCS} versioned draft prepare a policy workshop. The {WORKFLOW} publishes and assigns work only after senior management has approved that exact policy version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy evidence, meeting notes and later implementation actions are compiled and tracked in separate files.
tasks.enabler_now: Operational evidence can be assembled and document versions can be bound to a workflow decision.
tasks.still_hard: Risk appetite, fair treatment and the balance between growth and loss are leadership decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Senior managers can challenge a policy change against strategy, customer impact and accountability.

ambition.what: Review a named credit-policy exception pattern each quarter with its evidence and owner.

tasks.altitude: The officer maintains policy evidence quality and tests whether agreed controls work after rollout.

reach.task: Assess the operational impact of a proposed credit-policy change
reach.learn: Connect a control to observed exceptions and customer impact.

evidence.claim: Versioned records and workflow approvals can support a reviewable policy-change process.

assumptions: The boundary starts with a proposed policy change and ends with a published approved version and implementation work, not an automated change in lending decisions.

The policy contract contains policy ID, version, proposed rule, evidence link, impact statement, owner, approver, decision timestamp and implementation task; the policy owner supplies the rule and rationale.
A draft without a recorded senior-manager approval remains unpublished.
Native document versioning and approval routing are tested before custom code.
One hour per 100 focal-role baseline hours is allowed for policy-template and workflow-rule maintenance.
unknowns: Which senior-manager roles must approve each class of policy change.
How policy changes are tested before they affect new applications.
research_questions: Which policy exceptions recur often enough to justify a rule change?
How long does a policy change take from evidence to implemented control?

already_counted.description: Officer review of the evidence-backed policy draft

incremental.description: Maintain policy templates and approval routing

approvals.approved_version: approved policy version in the decision record

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The leadership discussion and policy judgement remain the main work; one upkeep hour per 100 focal-role baseline hours is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assist in selecting financial award candidates by certifying eligibility from electronic databases.

steps.what: Retrieve the candidate application, programme rules and authorised database records
Apply stated eligibility rules and identify missing, conflicting or exceptional evidence
Check the evidence and certify, defer or escalate the candidate's eligibility

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} gathers authorised records and evaluates the stated programme rules in the {CRM}. It shows missing evidence and rule exceptions, while the loan officer certifies eligibility or routes a difficult case to the award committee.
tasks.previous_blocker: The officer switches databases and manually marks each rule against the candidate's application.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured programme criteria can be tested consistently when source records and their dates are available.
tasks.still_hard: An exception, conflicting record or fairness concern cannot be resolved by the eligibility rule alone.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can recognise an edge case and make the evidence and uncertainty visible to the award committee.

ambition.what: Give applicants with missing eligibility evidence a precise list of what they can provide before committee review.

tasks.altitude: The officer audits rule exceptions and data gaps instead of copying database values into an eligibility sheet.

reach.task: Prepare an evidence-backed eligibility case for committee review
reach.learn: Map programme criteria to dated source records.

evidence.claim: Rules and arithmetic can be evaluated over structured financial records, with exceptions routed to a person.

assumptions: The boundary starts with a submitted candidate application and ends with a human eligibility certification or escalation, not a financial award decision.
The eligibility contract contains candidate ID, programme ID, rule version, source-record ID, source date, rule result, exception reason and certifier; authorised databases supply the factual fields.
A missing source, conflict or rule not represented in the workflow is escalated and never treated as eligibility.
Native case fields and rule configuration are tested before custom code.
Two hours per 100 focal-role baseline hours are allowed for rule updates, data mappings and exception review.
unknowns: Which eligibility rules can be represented without discretionary interpretation.
What independent review is required before an award is made.
research_questions: What proportion of applications fail due to missing evidence?
Which rules generate the most exceptions?

already_counted.description: Officer certification or escalation of rule results

incremental.description: Maintain programme rules and source mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Every certification remains human work; two upkeep hours per 100 baseline hours are deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select accounts eligible for a collection letter and exclude disputes, arrangements and protected cases
Populate the correct approved letter template with account facts, due amounts and payment instructions
Review the exact letter draft and authorise its send, hold or escalation
Send only the authorised letter version and write the send event to the account record

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} filters ineligible accounts and creates a versioned letter draft from approved {DOCS} content. It sends only the draft version explicitly authorised by the loan officer and logs that version on the {CRM} account.
tasks.previous_blocker: Officers move account values into letters, decide eligibility and send them through separate screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Account status rules and approved templates can be combined with a version-bound send approval.
tasks.still_hard: A disputed, vulnerable or recently paying customer may need a different response from a standard letter.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can judge whether the letter is fair, factually accurate and appropriate before it reaches a customer.

ambition.what: Give customers a prompt, accurate arrears letter that clearly states the amount, due date and available next contact.

tasks.altitude: The officer reviews why letters are held or escalated and improves the exception rules.

reach.task: Review an arrears case before collection action
reach.learn: Check a letter against account evidence, dispute state and payment arrangement.

evidence.claim: Rules can identify exceptions and approved templates can prepare financial documents, while a person reviews external action.

assumptions: The boundary starts with an overdue account and ends with an authorised letter version and recorded send event, not a collection decision.

The letter contract contains account ID, account-holder name, amount due, due date, template version, dispute state, arrangement state, draft hash, authorisation timestamp and send event; the account system provides the factual fields.
A changed draft hash or absent authorisation prevents sending.
Native template, approval and account-log features are tested before custom sending code.
Two hours per 100 focal-role baseline hours are allowed for template, eligibility-rule and send-failure maintenance.
unknowns: Which letters require a second signer or specialist approval.
What exact delivery channel and retention rules apply to collection letters.
research_questions: How often does an eligible draft get held by the officer?
Which exception state most often prevents a standard letter?

already_counted.description: Officer review and authorisation of letter draft

incremental.description: Maintain letter templates, eligibility rules and send-failure handling

approvals.approved_version: signed letter version and draft hash in letter authorisation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Officer review remains required for every letter; two upkeep hours per 100 baseline hours are deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate debt, available funds and payoff methods with estimated liquidation time.

steps.what: Collect debt balances, rates, minimum payments, income and available-funds inputs
Calculate total debt, disposable funds, alternative payment allocations and liquidation dates
Check assumptions and discuss which payoff method is realistic for the customer's circumstances
Store the chosen payoff illustration with assumptions and next review date

tasks.design: A deterministic calculation in {SPREADSHEET} or the {CRM} produces traceable payoff scenarios from validated balances and inputs. The loan officer tests assumptions with the customer and records the selected illustration rather than choosing a plan automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Debt balances and income are manually copied into a workbook for every scenario and assumptions are easy to lose.
tasks.enabler_now: Balance arithmetic and dated payoff scenarios can be calculated reproducibly from named inputs.
tasks.still_hard: A realistic payment plan depends on changing household circumstances and a sensitive conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can recognise when a calculated plan is not sustainable and help the customer seek the right support.

ambition.what: Give customers in arrears a clear payoff illustration with assumptions they can question before agreeing next steps.

tasks.altitude: The officer tests the quality of payoff assumptions and monitors where plans fail rather than rebuilding arithmetic.

reach.task: Discuss the sustainability of a repayment plan
reach.learn: Separate a calculation result from a customer's ability to maintain it.

evidence.claim: The digest identifies payment schedules and financial ratios as rules and arithmetic suited to deterministic calculation.

assumptions: The boundary starts with customer-provided and verified debt inputs and ends with a recorded payoff illustration, not a binding repayment agreement.

The scenario contract contains debt ID, balance, rate, minimum payment, income, available funds, allocation method, as-of date, assumed change and review date; the customer and account records provide the inputs.
Missing balances or an unstable income assumption prevent a recommendation and are discussed manually.
Native loan or debt-calculation features are tested before custom code.
One hour per 100 focal-role baseline hours is allowed for scenario-rule maintenance and calculation exceptions.
unknowns: Whether all debt balances can be verified through authorised sources.
Which payoff methods the lender may present without specialist debt advice.
research_questions: How often do balances or income assumptions change before the next review?
Which payoff scenarios are most often judged unaffordable by customers?

already_counted.description: Officer conversation about chosen payoff scenario

incremental.description: Maintain payoff rules and investigate calculation exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The customer discussion remains essential; one upkeep hour per 100 baseline hours is deducted.

role.altitude: Run a daily exception review across incomplete applications, credit evidence and authority routes.
reach: personal financial advisor: recognise when an applicant needs broader budgeting or debt advice
role.ambitious_version: Give more applicants a complete, understandable path from enquiry to an accountable lending decision.
